target_moa.text: Benzyl alcohol 5% lotion acts by stunning the respiratory spiracles of the louse so they remain open, allowing the lotion to occlude the breathing apparatus and cause asphyxiation and death of the louse

citations.quote: The purported mechanism of action for this product is a "stunning" of the respiratory spiracles of the louse such that they remain open, leading to blockage and subsequent asphyxiation.

Scanning electron microscopy demonstrated that when lice were exposed to the drug product their breathing spiracles remain open and allow liquid materials to occlude the breathing apparatus, resulting in death.
TRADENAME Lotion contains 5% benzyl alcohol and is supplied in 8 ounce polypropylene bottles.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>1% and more common than placebo): ocular irritation, application site irritation, and application site anesthesia and hypoesthesia. Application site irritation 2% (11/478) vs 1% (2/336) vehicle; application site anesthesia & hypoesthesia 2% (10/478) vs 0% vehicle. With onset after treatment: ocular irritation 6% (26/428) vs 1% (3/313) vehicle. No deaths and no serious adverse events were reported.

summary.text: NDA 22-129 was a 505(b)(2) application relying on literature references for some nonclinical toxicology information. It received an Approvable action on July 14, 2008, was addressed by a complete response submitted October 17, 2008, and was approved as a full (not accelerated) approval based on two randomized, vehicle-controlled trials. The pediatric study requirement for ages 6 months to 18 years was fulfilled.
